svg.title: B / TCP proxy NLB with Palo inspection
svg.desc: Managed TCP proxying can reach supported cross-VPC backends, but cannot inherit VM route tags.. Blue lines show application traffic; green dashed lines show return traffic; amber dotted lines show native health checks; gray dotted lines show resource or policy references. Purple lines show policy-directed inspection. Red lines show rejected or bypass paths. See adjacent ADR option for requirements.

g.text: 1. What happens if the RPs are replaced without changing the shared-VPC routing
Both regional Envoy sources can use the untagged baseline. The tagged regional PA override does not apply.
Managed Envoy sources do not have the RP VMs' route tags
2A. B1: Accept a central PA path
Keep one shared ingress routing domain. Change the regional failure boundary.
New ingress VPCs and supported end-to-end connectivity. Not just extra routes.
3. Native VM / NEG health checks bypass the frontend PA routing
A healthy backend does not prove PSC, proxy-only-subnet or PA transit.
Can fail while backends stay healthy
An application transaction must test PA transit.
MariaDB TLS can pass through unchanged. TCP termination
Client identity / PROXY protocol must be tested with the

PSC TCP producer support does not list regional internet
